newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge resume broadcasts, bash Pol Pot.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge resume broadcasts, bash Pol Pot.

text.p: The Khmer Rouge's clandestine radio station broke a four-day silence and resumed broadcasting on Tuesday with a statement accusing guerrilla strongman Pol Pot of betraying his comrades.

"From the 9th to 14th of June, there were betrayals by Pol Pot. But this problem has been solved quietly by the unity forces," said an announcement read during broadcasts on Monday evening and Tuesday morning.

Rebel radio, which appeared to be in the hands of anti-Pol Pot guerrillas, said the statement was that of a provisional government loyal to nominal Khmer Rouge leader Khieu Samphan and his National Solidarity Party.

Khieu Samphan, who has been the president of the Khmer Rouge's provisional government for years, is reported to be a hostage of guerrilla leader Pol Pot, said to be on the run after fleeing his northern Anlong Veng stronghold.
Khieu Samphan recently announced that he wanted to form a political alliance with Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh ahead of elections due in 1998.
The prince has welcomed the idea.
